title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Verdant Therapeutics
next_steps: Redwood to send updated pricing for 3-region Dedicated commit by 2025-12-05
Verdant to confirm preferred additional regions (eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1) by 2025-12-08
SE to run 48hr perf benchmark on Verdant sample workload and share spreadsheet link
Schedule legal follow-up for contract extension terms week of 12/15
action_items: Carlos - run 48hr perf run and share benchmark spreadsheet (due 2025-12-09)
Maya - send updated pricing and renewal term options (due 2025-12-05)
Amira - consolidate procurement questions and share PO process doc (due 2025-12-08)
Jared - prepare SSO/SAML & SOC2 docs bundle and share link (due 2025-12-04)
summary: Renewal and expansion check-in focused on capacity upgrade (Dedicated GPUs), adding EU and APAC regions, and negotiation timeline for contract extension. Customer is leaning toward a 12-month commit with a 20% capacity increase and wants a pilot in ap-southeast-1 before full commit. Security and data residency questions were raised; Redwood confirmed SOC2 and KMS options and offered a 48hr benchmark run.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for jumping on, quick check-in about renewal and expansion, we have about 40 minutes, so we'll go through capacity needs, regions, timeline, and any security/legal asks.
[00:12] Lena (Verdant): thanks maya, yeah we wanted to start with our capacity numbers — we've been seeing a 30% q/q growth in token usage and the hosted tier is starting to show limits during peak biology simulation windows, so we're exploring Dedicated.
[00:25] Carlos (Redwood SE): cool, can you give a sense of peak p99 latency and desired throughput? also are you using KV cache heavily or mostly single shot prompts? (sorry kv cash, transcription)
[00:37] Lena: peak p99 is ~620ms on hosted right now for our 2k token seq, and we need to get below 400ms ideally, throughput target is about 250 concurrent reqs at peak. We do use prefix caching for a subset of workflows, and long running KV cache for embeddings retriever.
[00:54] Ethan (Verdant): key ask is also data residency - our european trials require model inference in eu-west, and we're piloting APAC for a partner in singapore, so would need eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 availability.
[01:10] Maya: understood. For Dedicated we can allocate reserved GPU pools in those regions; the typical approach is a 12-month commit for predictability, and then we can add burst capacity. Quick note on pricing: we have a committed and burst model — I'll follow up with updated numbers.
[01:23] Amira (Procurement): timeline — we want to finalize terms by mid-December so legal can onboard before Q1. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[01:32] Maya: not from our side, we just need to align on commit size and regions. Jared will prepare SOC2 and SSO docs.
[01:38] Jared (CSM): I'll share SOC2 report, audit logs spec, and SAML config examples after the call.
[01:45] Noah (Infra): question on key management — do you support customer KMS/HSM, and can keys be region-specific?
[01:52] Carlos: yes we support customer-managed keys (KMS) and can scope per-region encryption at rest with a customer key; in private we can support HSM setups for on-prem. Note: some details differ by infra provider, we'll add specifics to the security bundle.
[02:08] Lena: great. on perf, would you recommend quantization? we've been using fp16 on some models but worried about quality regressions for certain structured outputs.
[02:17] Carlos: we can provide quantization profiles per model; our Optimize team has seen minimal quality delta for embeddings and many generation tasks when using 4-bit quant with calibration. For structured outputs we can run evals on your prompt set as part of the benchmark.
[02:34] Ethan: also want to mention competitor evals — some interns ran quick runs on Bedrock and Anthropic and said cost looked lower but latency was higher. We're not fully trusting that test yet.
[02:47] Maya: totally, that's why we'll run a comparative benchmark if you want. We can do a Redwood-hosted run on your sample data and share token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
[02:58] Amira: procurement needs: a paper trail for renewal options, early-termination clauses, and clear invoicing cadence. Can you send examples?
[03:06] Maya: yes we'll include contract examples — options for 12 vs 24 month, invoice monthly or net-30.
[03:12] Ravi (SRE): small infra question — will adding regions require network peering setup or is it all on Redwood managed VPCs? Also what about cross-region KV sync?
[03:22] Carlos: for Dedicated we provide managed VPCs; you can choose to have peering to your VPC or use VPC endpoints. Cross-region KV sync is supported but it's an additional config for low-latency replication, we can design a topology that keeps keys local for residency and replicate meta data only.
[03:40] Lena: ok, so proposed plan from our side: increase commit by ~20% capacity, add eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 as pilot region (full roll after pilot), and extend contract 12 months with possibility to convert to 24 at a later discount. Are there any technical risks?
[03:56] Carlos: technical risks are minimal; main items are model selection and kernel optimizations for specific seq lengths — we prefer to run the 48hr benchmarking on your workload to validate latency SLOs and cost. Also if you want sub-400ms p99 for 2k tokens we may recommend a specific GPU class and batching config.
[04:18] Ethan: timeline check — if we sign by Dec 12 can you have region capacity ready by Jan 20?
[04:25] Maya: yes that aligns with typical provisioning times but we'll flag for priority. For APAC there might be a few days extra depending on cloud partner capacity; we'll confirm in the rush schedule.
[04:38] Lena: on the bench marking, what metrics will you provide? we need p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and cold start numbers, also perf under burst.
[04:50] Carlos: we'll provide p50/p95/p99, token cost breakdown, GPU utilization, KV hit rates, and a simulated burst test with autoscaling behavior. We'll share a google sheet link (we usually use a perf spreadsheet) — note: link will be redwood.com/bench/verdant-2025 (placeholder).
[05:07] Amira: can you also include a sample SLA for Dedicated? We need uptime, maintenance windows and rollback policy.
[05:16] Jared: yes SLA and maintenance windows - we have standard 99.9% SLA for Dedicated; maintenance windows are scheduled with advanced notice and we have fallback routes to hosted variants. We'll include the rollback/canary policy too.
[05:28] Ethan: on security, will audit logs be accessible in our console or do we get a syslog feed?
[05:34] Carlos: both options — we can stream to your SIEM via syslog or provide S3+encryption exports and console access for on-demand queries.
[05:44] Lena: small nit — we've seen some transcription oddities in the past, so when Jared sends docs can you make sure the SSO examples include our IdP (Okta) specifics?
[05:53] Jared: absolutely, we'll include Okta SAML mapping examples.
[06:00] Maya: ok open floor for any final Qs before recapping next steps.
[06:04] Noah: one more — any implications for model updates/rollouts? we run nightly model refreshes and want deterministic rollbacks during eval degradations.
[06:12] Carlos: rollout controls are supported — canary deploys, A/B tests and automatic fallback policies. We can pin model versions per route and schedule rollouts outside of peak windows, we also keep image versioning for deterministic rollback.
[06:28] Ethan: perfect.
[06:30] Lena: thanks, this is productive.
[06:33] Maya: recap — action items: Carlos will run 48hr perf benchmark on your sample set; I'll send updated pricing for a 12-month commit with 20% capacity increase and options for 24 months; Jared will send SOC2/SSO/SAML docs and SLA; Amira will share procurement timeline. We'll aim to have a decision and signed terms by Dec 12.
[06:51] Amira: noted.
[06:53] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and the spreadsheet. bye.
[06:58] End of recording (approx 42 minutes).
